Table 1 shows the physical properties of copper, Cu.

| Property | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Melting point | 1085 °C | Very high |
| Solubility in water | Insoluble | Insoluble |
| Electrical conductivity | 5.96 × 10⁷ S/m at 20 °C | Excellent |
| Malleability | Malleable | Can be shaped |
| Hardness | 3.0 Mohs | Moderately hard |

Copper wire is widely used in household electrical wiring. The copper is drawn into thin wires and carries electric current throughout a house.

Describe TWO physical properties of copper and link these two physical properties to their use in household electrical wiring.
questions.expectedAnswer: Copper has excellent electrical conductivity (5.96 × 10⁷ S/m) so it efficiently carries current.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Describes the structure, relative strength of attractive forces, and the physical properties of copper, and how these link to its use in electrical wiring or allow the wiring to function.

questions.text: Explain these TWO physical properties with reference to the structure and bonding of copper.
questions.expectedAnswer: Copper is a metallic solid with a 3D lattice of Cu⁺ cations surrounded by delocalised electrons
questions.markingGuide: Merit: Explains how the structure, relative strength of attractive forces between the atoms, and how the physical properties of copper make it suitable for use in electrical wiring. Some aspects of the explanation are incomplete.

questions.text: Evaluate how copper will behave when used as household electrical wiring by linking the TWO physical properties to the structure and bonding.

questions.markingGuide: Excellence: Evaluates the structure, relative strength of attractive forces between the atoms, and how the physical properties of copper enable effective electrical wiring through conductivity and the ability to be drawn into thin wires.

questions.text:
Table 2 shows physical properties of nitrogen gas, N₂, and oxygen gas, O₂.

| Property | Nitrogen, N₂ | Oxygen, O₂ |
|---|---|---|
| Boiling point at 1 atm | −196 °C | −183 °C |
| Density at 20 °C | 1.25 kg/m³ | 1.43 kg/m³ |
| Electrical conductivity | Insulator | Insulator |

Food packaging sometimes replaces the air inside with pure nitrogen gas to keep food fresh for longer. Nitrogen gas is non-reactive and displaces oxygen that would cause the food to spoil.

Describe TWO physical properties of nitrogen gas and link these two physical properties to its use in keeping food fresh in sealed packaging.
questions.expectedAnswer: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point (−196 °C) so it is a gas at room temperature.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Describes the structure, relative strength of attractive forces, and a physical property of nitrogen gas, and how this links to its use in food packaging.

questions.text:
Pounamu (New Zealand greenstone or nephrite jade) is a mineral prized in Māori culture for making tools and ornaments. Pounamu is a silicate mineral with a fibrous crystalline structure.

Table 3 shows properties of pounamu and other materials.

| Material | Hardness (Mohs) | Solubility in water |
|---|---|---|
| Pounamu (jade) | 6.0–6.5 | Insoluble |
| Obsidian (volcanic glass) | 5.0–5.5 | Insoluble |
| Calcite (limestone mineral) | 3.0 | Slightly soluble |
| Quartz | 7.0 | Insoluble |

Pounamu was traditionally shaped into cutting tools (toki) and personal adornments (hei-tiki). It is very tough and resists chipping.

Describe TWO physical properties of pounamu and link these two physical properties to their use in making tools and adornments.
questions.expectedAnswer: Pounamu is hard (6.0–6.5 Mohs) so it can hold a sharp edge for cutting tools.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Describes the structure, relative strength of attractive forces, and the physical properties of pounamu and how it links to its usage/suitability as a tool or adornment.

questions.text: Explain these TWO physical properties, with reference to the structure and bonding of pounamu.
